en.title: Global Macro — China's orders retreat as Europe's output slows and energy risks outlast the bond rally
en.deck: China's October factory and export-order surveys fell below 50, Europe's Q3 GDP growth slowed and US yields eased; uneven demand meets persistent energy risks.
en.regime: Uneven global expansion with weaker Chinese order diffusion and persistent energy cost risks.
en.key_risk: Industrial demand weakens while energy import costs and borrower-specific credit costs stay elevated.

producer_checks.information_cutoff: 2026-10-31 05:00 BRT (08:00 UTC); China NBS 31 Oct 09:30 CST released 30 Oct 22:30 BRT; 30 Oct US/EU completed releases and sessions.
producer_checks.novelty: Compared 28 Oct Korean AI memory contracts, 29 Oct Fed/BoC divergence, 30 Oct US GDP/income. New NBS October PMI by size and export orders plus Eurostat Q3 GDP and Sep unemployment and 30 Oct US Treasury curve; distinct thesis on geographically uneven goods demand.
producer_checks.source_check: 14 numbered references in each language; primary NBS, Eurostat, Treasury, BEA, ECB, Fed, World Bank, ICI. Reuters used only for qualified conflict/settlement context. Dates, frequencies and conditional forecasts distinguished.
producer_checks.visual_signature: EN/PT each 1 evidence table, 5 quantitative charts with identical values, 1 three-chain flow, 1 five-region map. All chart values trace to NBS, Eurostat and Treasury.
producer_checks.bilingual_parity: Same 14 reference URLs, numerical evidence, uncertainty qualifiers, five chart series and conditional scenario logic in both languages.
producer_checks.research_depth: Substantive multi-regional argument; independent mechanisms, contrary evidence, falsifiers, stock-flow distinctions, observation vintages.

contrary_evidence: Chinese high-technology manufacturing subsectors above 53 and large manufacturers at 50.2; one-month survey can be affected by holidays.
Euro-area real GDP still expanded 0.4% q/q in Q3; Irish and Spanish growth show heterogeneity.
US Q3 real GDP rose 3.4% annualised, inconsistent with a uniform global contraction.
limitations: China PMI is a diffusion index and not measured export volumes, factory output growth or SME credit access.
Eurostat GDP is preliminary, country composition and annualisation differ from US GDP.
No independently verified new Gulf shipping throughput, insurance costs or borrower-level credit spreads.
Cross-border capital flow attribution unavailable; ICI money fund asset change cannot identify international reallocations.
